summary: Martin Willson (d. 2005) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers including Yeshe Thubten, Lama Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, Geshe Thubten Loden, Zasep Tulku Rinpoche, Geshe Rabten, Geshe Jampa Tegchok, and Geshe Lhundub Sopa.

Martina Draszczyk works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under MA supervisor Lambert Schmithausen, earned her Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna (attested 2012), and served as a researcher there.

Martine Kropman is an Indologist who conducted doctoral research at the University of Groningen. She became an external PhD candidate at Leiden University, studying under doctoral supervisor Peter C. Bisschop (attested 2026).

Martino Dibeltulo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed his PhD at the University of Michigan, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Donald S. Lopez Jr., and also studied under mentor Ester Bianchi.

Marvin Eisenberg (1922–2016) was a scholar of history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Pennsylvania (~1939–1943) and Princeton University (~1946–1954), and spent his career on the faculty at the University of Michigan (~1949–1993).
Mary Anne Cartelli specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Columbia University (attested 1999), where she studied under doctoral supervisor Philip B. Yampolsky.

Mary Clabaugh Wright (1917–1970) worked in Sinology, history, and archaeology. Educated at Vassar and Radcliffe, she was curator at the Hoover Institution (~1946–1959), taught at Stanford (1947), and held associate and full professorships at Yale (1959, 1964).

Mary Evelyn Tucker (b. 1949) specializes in religious studies, Sinology, and Japanology. After doctoral studies at Columbia (~1978–1985), she was Professor of Religion at Bucknell (~1989–2005) and became a professor at Yale around 2006.

Mary Haas (1910–1996) was a linguist. She studied at Earlham College, the University of Chicago, and Yale University, working under Edward Sapir (~1930–1935), before serving on the faculty at the University of California, Berkeley (~1947–1977).
Mary Jaksch (b. 1947) works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at the University of Sunderland under Peter Harvey (attested 2007) and also studied under traditional teacher Ross Bolleter.

Mary Margaret McCabe (b. 1948) is a philosopher. Educated at Newnham College and the University of Cambridge, she was a Fellow in Classics at Murray Edwards College (1981–1990) and Professor at King's College London (1990–2014).

Mary Shepherd Slusser (1918–2017) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. She earned degrees from Michigan and Columbia, later working for the U.S. Department of State (1951–1958) and the National Museum of African Art (1971–1978).
Marybeth White works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She completed her undergraduate studies at York University and was a doctoral candidate at Wilfrid Laurier University (attested 2006).

Maryla Falk (1906–1980) was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. She held a post at the University of Warsaw (~1933–1939) and was a Fellow of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland (1974).

Marylin Martin Rhie specializes in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Sinology. She studied under mentors Harrie Vanderstappen and Pramod Chandra, and served as a professor at Smith College (attested 1986).

Masaaki Chikusa (1930–2015) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Kyoto University, he served there as assistant (1968) and professor (1981–1993) before becoming a professor at Otani University (~1993–2001).

Masaaki Hattori (b. 1924) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. Educated at Kyoto University and the University of Calcutta, he taught at Kyoto University (1955; 1961–1988) and became a professor at Osaka Gakuin University in 1989.

Masaaki Nitta (b. 1936) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed doctoral coursework at the University of Tokyo. He served as a professor at Fukui Prefectural College (attested 1983–1991) and Fukui Prefectural University (attested 1988).

Masaaki Nohnin (b. 1949) specializes in Buddhist studies. A student of Gadjin Nagao, he served on the faculty at Ryukoku University as an assistant professor (attested 2003) and later as a professor (attested 2013–2014).
Masaaki Tsuchiya (b. 1960) is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Kokugakuin University and holds a post at Senshu University.
